instruction: Navigate to the Unit Tests topic page on this CS50 Python course website.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated CS50 Python course weeks 1-9 sequentially, downloading lecture PDFs from each week page. Files downloaded to Chrome default directory instead of /home/user/lecture_slides/.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome to specific URLs, click PDF links on web pages, navigate through course week pages sequentially, identify and interact with CS50 course website sidebar
metadata.failure_analysis: Model downloaded PDFs to Chrome default Downloads folder instead of the specified /home/user/lecture_slides/ directory. Never attempted to change download location or move files.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests navigation to a non-adjacent week page (Week 5 from Week 0). Model demonstrated this capability in the trajectory, so this verifies reliable navigation to a specific topic.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating from Week 0 to Week 5 (Unit Tests) on CS50 Python course. Evaluator checks active tab URL matches the Week 5 pattern.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (active_url_from_accessTree) correctly extracts the active Chrome tab URL, which is exactly the state needed to verify navigation.
Metric (is_expected_url_pattern_match) correctly receives the rules dict and accesses rules['expected'] to get regex patterns, matching the framework's type='rule' convention.
Expected regex pattern 'cs50\.harvard\.edu/python/.*weeks/5' correctly identifies the CS50 Python Week 5 (Unit Tests) page URL.
Single-step navigation task is fully covered by checking the final URL - no missing verification steps.
Data flow is correct: getter returns string URL -> metric handles string type -> regex match returns 1.0 on success.
